Debuted in 1994's Sonic the Hedgehog 3 as an antagonist tricked by Dr. Eggman before becoming Sonic's steadfast ally
Possesses immense physical strength, spiked knuckles that smash stone, and the ability to glide through air and scale walls
Last surviving member of the ancient Echidna clan dedicated to maintaining spiritual equilibrium across Mobius

facts_and_myths.claim: Knuckles was originally intended to speak with a Jamaican accent and have green fur during early conceptual design phases.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Early design documents from Sonic Team experimented with green fur and Jamaican reggae influences before settling on red fur and spiked gloves.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The unique lock-on cartridge technology of Sonic & Knuckles allowed players to insert Sonic 2 or Sonic 3 on top of the cart to play as Knuckles.

facts_and_myths.claim: Knuckles is biologically unable to jump as high as Sonic because his dreadlocks are filled with heavy spiked armor.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Knuckles jumps slightly lower than Sonic in gameplay purely for game balancing due to his powerful climbing and gliding mechanics, not because of armor in his dreadlocks.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The white crescent mark on his chest was originally envisioned to resemble the Nike swoosh before being modified.

name: Dr. Eggman
visual_anchor: Villainous vertical 9:16 digital illustration of Dr. Eggman laughing maniacally from his hovering Egg Mobile cockpit, twirling his giant bushy ginger mustache with glowing mechanical badnik robots and towering factory smokestacks behind him.
core_traits: Egg-shaped human mad scientist possessing a genius IQ of 300 and the primary archenemy of Sonic the Hedgehog
Obsessed with collecting the Chaos Emeralds to conquer the globe and construct his dream amusement empire Eggmanland
Traps woodland animals inside robotic infantry drones called Badniks to fuel his mechanized conquest legions
Pilots a versatile round hovercraft known as the Egg Mobile, often retrofitted with giant wrecking balls and laser cannons

facts_and_myths.claim: Dr. Eggman's round physique and pajamas were originally pitched to Sega executives as a candidate for the company's heroic mascot.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Designer Naoto Ohshima submitted the character as a hero candidate wearing pajamas; when Sonic won, the team liked the design so much they repurposed him into the main villain.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: In Western territories he was named Doctor Ivo Robotnik until Sega unified his canon name as Doctor Eggman starting with Sonic Adventure in 1998.

facts_and_myths.claim: Dr. Eggman is an extraterrestrial alien who landed on Earth after fleeing a devastated machine planet.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Eggman is canonically human, the grandson of the renowned brilliant Earth scientist Professor Gerald Robotnik, creator of Shadow the Hedgehog.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Eggman's mustache was inspired by President Theodore Roosevelt and caricatured German militaristic styles.

name: Shadow the Hedgehog
visual_anchor: Dramatic vertical 9:16 composition of Shadow the Hedgehog standing on the exterior hull of the Space Colony ARK, arms folded grimly as red energy sparks crackle from his hover skates, clutching a green Chaos Emerald in deep space.
core_traits: Genetically engineered black-and-crimson hedgehog created fifty years ago by Professor Gerald Robotnik as the Ultimate Lifeform
Debuted as a central antihero and Sonic's dark foil in 2001's Dreamcast title Sonic Adventure 2
Propelled at supersonic speeds using rocket-powered Air Shoes and can manipulate space-time through Chaos Control
Driven by a solemn vow to protect humanity made to his departed childhood companion Maria Robotnik

facts_and_myths.claim: Shadow was originally intended to die permanently at the end of his debut appearance in Sonic Adventure 2.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Sonic Adventure 2 was written as a one-off story where Shadow sacrifices himself falling into Earth's atmosphere, but overwhelming fan popularity prompted Sonic Team to revive him in Sonic Heroes.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: During development of Sonic Adventure 2, Shadow was codenamed Terios, which translates roughly to reflection of.

facts_and_myths.claim: Shadow is a direct physical clone created in a laboratory from Sonic the Hedgehog's DNA.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Shadow was engineered aboard the Space Colony ARK using the alien DNA of Black Doom fifty years before Sonic was even born, meaning he is not a clone of Sonic.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Shadow wielded real firearms and drove military motorcycles in his self-titled 2005 spin-off game Shadow the Hedgehog.

name: Mega Man
visual_anchor: Classic vertical 9:16 retro-futuristic illustration of Mega Man sliding across a metallic futuristic factory floor, blue armored arm cannon Mega Buster charging a bright turquoise plasma blast surrounded by flying robot sentries.
core_traits: Iconic humanoid robot created by Dr. Thomas Light in 200X to defeat the rogue robotic forces of Dr. Albert Wily
Equipped with the arm-mounted Mega Buster plasma cannon and the unique Variable Weapon System to copy defeated bosses' powers
Debuted on the Nintendo Entertainment System in 1987 as Capcom's legendary action-platforming mascot
Accompanied into combat by his faithful cybernetic canine companion Rush and robotic sister Roll

facts_and_myths.claim: Mega Man was colored blue because the Nintendo Entertainment System had more shades of blue available in its color palette than any other color.
facts_and_myths.explanation: The NES color palette had 54 total colors, with shades of blue being the most varied and detailed, allowing Capcom designers to create crisp shading on an 8-bit sprite.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: In Japan he is named Rockman as a musical pun with his robotic sister Roll, making Rock and Roll.

facts_and_myths.claim: Keiji Inafune was the sole creative designer who invented the original concept and sprite of Mega Man.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Keiji Inafune has clarified that Akira Kitamura originally created the concept and sprite design for Mega Man, while Inafune refined the art and drew the character illustrations.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The infamous North American NES cover art featured an awkwardly posed middle-aged man in a yellow-and-blue suit holding a real pistol.

name: Pac-Man
visual_anchor: Vibrant vertical 9:16 arcade artwork of the bright yellow spherical character Pac-Man chomping glowing power pellets down a dark neon-blue maze, chased closely by colorful ghostly apparitions Blinky and Pinky under neon arcade lighting.
core_traits: Legendary yellow pizza-shaped arcade icon created by Toru Iwatani and released by Namco in 1980
Navigates enclosed neon labyrinth mazes eating dots, fruit bonuses, and hunting flashing ghost monsters
Consumes glowing Power Pellets to temporarily turn his ghost pursuers blue and vulnerable to being eaten
Hunted by four distinct spectral adversaries named Blinky, Pinky, Inky, and Clyde, each governed by unique AI routing

facts_and_myths.claim: Pac-Man's original Japanese arcade release was titled Puck Man, derived from the Japanese phrase paku-paku.
facts_and_myths.explanation: The name came from paku-paku taberu, describing the sound of opening and closing one's mouth while eating; it was altered to Pac-Man in North America to prevent arcade vandals from altering the P to an F.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Designer Toru Iwatani famously drew inspiration for the character's round shape after taking a single slice out of a whole pizza.

facts_and_myths.claim: The four ghosts in Pac-Man pursue the player with identical chasing algorithms to ensure relentless pressure.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Each ghost operates under completely different behavioral logic: Blinky pursues directly, Pinky ambushes four tiles ahead, Inky flanks based on Blinky's position, and Clyde wanders away when close.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: A perfect game of Pac-Man requires completing all 256 stages without dying once, reaching the famous half-screen glitch with a maximum score of 3,333,360 points.

name: Crash Bandicoot
visual_anchor: Exuberant vertical 9:16 action portrait of Crash Bandicoot mid-spin in bright blue denim jeans and red sneakers, shattering wooden Wumpa fruit crates along a sun-drenched jungle pathway alongside the levitating tiki mask Aku Aku.
core_traits: Genetically enhanced eastern barred bandicoot created by Naughty Dog and released on the Sony PlayStation in 1996
Battles the nefarious mad scientist Dr. Neo Cortex across the fictional Wumpa Islands to thwart world domination
Signature combat and movement abilities include a high-speed whirlwind spin, slide attack, and high belly flop
Guided and protected throughout perilous obstacle gauntlets by the ancient wooden witch doctor spirit mask Aku Aku

facts_and_myths.claim: Crash Bandicoot was codenamed Willy the Wombat during early development before the team selected a bandicoot.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Naughty Dog co-founders Andy Gavin and Jason Rubin initially created Willy the Wombat on paper before choosing a real-life obscure Australian marsupial, the bandicoot, and naming him Crash after his crate-smashing antics.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Crash was conceived intentionally as a cool, irreverent mascot to serve as Sony's unofficial counter-mascot to Nintendo's Mario and Sega's Sonic.

facts_and_myths.claim: The fruit that Crash Bandicoot collects in every stage are tropical golden apples.
facts_and_myths.explanation: The fruit collected by Crash are fictional Wumpa fruit, which resemble a hybrid blend of an apple and a mango with purple juice.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Collecting 100 Wumpa fruit grants an extra life, similar to collecting 100 coins in Mario or 100 rings in Sonic.

name: Spyro the Dragon
visual_anchor: Lively vertical 9:16 fantasy scene of Spyro the Dragon gliding across lush green floating islands, breathing bright crimson flames at crystal statues while his golden companion Sparx the Dragonfly hovers glowing overhead against pastel skies.
core_traits: Energetic young purple dragon created by Insomniac Games and debuted on the Sony PlayStation in 1998
Embarks on quests across the Dragon Realms and Avalar to rescue elder dragons trapped in crystal by the evil Gnasty Gnorc
Combines fiery dragon breath, horns-first charging tackles, and aerial gliding to defeat foes and traverse open 3D realms
Accompanied by Sparx the Dragonfly, who acts as a loyal companion and visual health indicator through his glowing colors

facts_and_myths.claim: Spyro was originally designed with green scales before Insomniac Games changed his color to purple.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Developers colored Spyro green in prototype builds, but quickly realized he completely blended into the green grass textures of the game's meadows, prompting the switch to purple for contrast.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Stewart Copeland, the legendary drummer of the rock band The Police, composed the entire original musical soundtrack for Spyro the Dragon.

facts_and_myths.claim: Spyro was created as a direct spin-off character from the Skylanders toy-to-life video game franchise.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Spyro starred in his own acclaimed 3D platforming trilogy on the original PlayStation starting in 1998, thirteen years before Skylanders: Spyro's Adventure was released in 2011.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Insomniac Games used NASA flight physics algorithms to program the camera angles and glide mechanics in Spyro.

name: Rayman
visual_anchor: Whimsical vertical 9:16 composition of Rayman winding up his disembodied white-gloved fist for a projectile punch, purple torso hovering in mid-air with his blonde hair spinning like a helicopter propeller in the enchanted Dream Forest.
core_traits: Cheerful, limbless magical hero created by French game designer Michel Ancel and published by Ubisoft in 1995
Characterized by having floating hands, feet, and head with no connected arms or legs attached to his torso
Propels himself over chasms using his signature helicopter hair spin and launches telescopic winding fist strikes
Protects the Glade of Dreams and the Great Protoon from villains such as Mr. Dark, Admiral Razorbeard, and Andre the Dark Lum

facts_and_myths.claim: Rayman was designed without arms, legs, or a neck primarily due to technological hardware limitations.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Michel Ancel omitted limbs because animating the joints and rendering connected appendages exceeded the processing capabilities and memory budgets of 1990s hardware.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Rayman's sidekick Globox was voiced by famous actor and comedian John Leguizamo in Rayman 3: Hoodlum Havoc.

facts_and_myths.claim: The chaotic Raving Rabbids characters were originally designed as harmless peaceful sidekicks for Rayman.
facts_and_myths.explanation: The Rabbids were designed from the start as comedic alien antagonists who invaded Rayman's peaceful world, eventually eclipsing him in popularity to launch their own spin-off franchise.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The original 1995 Rayman game on Atari Jaguar and PlayStation is considered one of the most notoriously punishing platformers ever made.

name: Cloud Strife
visual_anchor: Spiky blond mercenary wielding a colossal broad Buster Sword across his shoulder, standing atop a rainy Midgar steel girder with glowing mako-infused cyan eyes, dark purple SOLDIER uniform, cinematic atmospheric volumetric lighting, 9:16 vertical composition.
core_traits: Former Shinra infantryman who falsely believed himself to be an elite first-class SOLDIER due to severe mako poisoning and Jenova cell trauma
Iconic wielder of the massive iron Buster Sword originally passed down from Angeal Hewley and Zack Fair
Hired as a mercenary by the eco-terrorist cell AVALANCHE to bomb Shinra Electric Power Company mako reactors in Midgar
Rides the customized Fenrir motorcycle and unleashes the devastating signature multi-strike Limit Break Omnislash

facts_and_myths.claim: Cloud was legitimately accepted and officially promoted to SOLDIER First Class by the Shinra Electric Power Company.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Cloud never qualified for SOLDIER due to mental instability and remained an ordinary Shinra infantryman; his memories as a First Class operative were an identity delusion triggered by Jenova cells after Zack Fair's sacrifice.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: During the Nibelheim incident where he struck down Sephiroth, Cloud was wearing a standard faceless Shinra infantry helmet.

facts_and_myths.claim: Cloud Strife's famous Buster Sword was originally designed with a single slot for Materia before being expanded to two paired slots.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Early design drafts for Final Fantasy VII gave the Buster Sword only one Materia slot before battle designers decided that paired Materia combinations were crucial to core gameplay mechanics.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The Buster Sword has two distinct holes near the hilt, allowing two linked Materia orbs to interact and enhance magical abilities.

name: Sephiroth
visual_anchor: Silver-haired fallen warrior brandishing a ridiculously long Masamune nodachi blade, surrounded by swirling fiery embers of burning Nibelheim, a single black feathered wing unfurled from his right shoulder in dramatic vertical 9:16 portrait framing.
core_traits: Celebrated war hero and top-ranking First Class SOLDIER who discovered he was the product of inhumane scientific experiments injecting Jenova cells into a fetus
Wields the iconic six-to-eight foot long Masamune katana with superhuman speed and effortless precision
Burns Nibelheim to the ground and descends into the Lifestream before attempting to summon Meteor to wound the planet and ascend as a god
Haunts the subconscious of Cloud Strife across decades while accompanied by the Latin choral theme One-Winged Angel

facts_and_myths.claim: Sephiroth's biological mother was the extraterrestrial calamity known as Jenova.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Sephiroth was biologically born to human Shinra scientist Lucrecia Crescent and Professor Hojo, who injected Jenova cells into Lucrecia's womb while pregnant as part of the Jenova Project.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Lucrecia preserved herself in a crystalline cave within the waterfall grotto of Mount Nibel to escape her guilt.

facts_and_myths.claim: The iconic musical theme One-Winged Angel contains Latin lyrics inspired by medieval secular poems from Carmina Burana.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Composer Nobuo Uematsu handpicked lines from medieval poetic texts in Carmina Burana and set them to rapid staccato orchestral and rock arrangements to symbolize Sephiroth's madness.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: It was the very first piece of music in the Final Fantasy franchise to feature real recorded human vocal choruses on the PlayStation 1.

name: Tifa Lockhart
visual_anchor: Athletic female martial artist with long brown hair styled in a dolphin tail, wearing leather combat gloves and tank top, launching a devastating aerial punch amidst glowing neon signs of Midgar Sector 7 slums in a cinematic 9:16 vertical poster.
core_traits: Childhood friend of Cloud Strife from Nibelheim and skilled martial artist trained under the legendary master Zangan
Runs the Seventh Heaven tavern in the Sector 7 slums of Midgar as a covert base of operations for the resistance group AVALANCHE
Serves as the emotional anchor of the party and helps Cloud reconstruct his shattered true memories inside the Lifestream
Fights exclusively with bare knuckles, clawed knuckles, and acrobatic martial arts Limit Breaks such as Dolphin Blow and Final Heaven

facts_and_myths.claim: Tifa Lockhart was killed during the Nibelheim incident when Sephiroth slashed her across the chest.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Although Sephiroth severely wounded her with his Masamune blade, her martial arts mentor Zangan rescued her from the burning reactor and brought her to Midgar to undergo life-saving surgery.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Zangan left behind a hidden letter to Tifa describing her miraculous recovery and passing on his ultimate technique, Final Heaven.

facts_and_myths.claim: Tifa Lockhart was intentionally designed with dark clothing and martial arts brawling to contrast sharply with Aerith's bright, magical persona.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Character designer Tetsuya Nomura deliberately created Tifa as an athletic brawler with a dark outfit and tough exterior but gentle interior, contrasting Aerith's feminine floral dress and spunky demeanor.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Early development sketches portrayed Tifa wearing suspenders and combat boots to emphasize her practical agility in urban slums.

name: Aerith Gainsborough
visual_anchor: Gentle young woman in a pink dress and red jacket kneeling in prayer with clasped hands beneath radiant heavenly light beams filtering through a ruined Midgar church filled with yellow blossoms, captured in ethereal 9:16 vertical orientation.
core_traits: The sole surviving pure-blooded Cetra, an ancient race gifted with the ability to communicate directly with the Planet and hear its spiritual voice
Grew up in the Sector 5 slums of Midgar selling fresh yellow flowers while evading capture by Shinra's covert investigative unit, the Turks
Possesses the legendary White Materia concealed within her pink hair ribbon, which holds the divine protection magic Holy
Travels to the Forgotten Capital to summon Holy to stop Meteor before meeting a tragic fate at the blade of Sephiroth

facts_and_myths.claim: Aerith can be revived in the original 1997 Final Fantasy VII through an elaborate sequence of secret inputs and underwater Materia quests.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Aerith's death is a permanent and unalterable narrative event intended to convey the profound, sudden finality of real grief; all revival rumors on 1990s internet forums were fabricated hoaxes.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Early game data left behind unused code where Aerith had battle dialog for later dungeons, fueling playground myths for decades.

facts_and_myths.claim: Aerith's name was officially localized as Aeris in the original English release of Final Fantasy VII due to a transliteration quirk.
facts_and_myths.explanation: The Japanese spelling Earisu was phonetically transliterated into English as Aeris in 1997, but later Square Enix games and Kingdom Hearts restored her intended canonical name Aerith.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The name Aerith is a near-anagram of the word Earth, symbolizing her bond with the Cetra and the Planet.

name: Noctis Lucis Caelum
visual_anchor: Young black-haired monarch in a tailored black suit throwing a spectral crystalline royal arm forward to warp-strike across a neon city street under stormy twilight skies, phantom ethereal blades floating in orbit around him, vertical 9:16 aspect ratio.
core_traits: Crown Prince and sole heir to the throne of Lucis, destined by the Crystal to become the True King and purge the Starscourge
Embarks on a road trip across the continent of Eos alongside his loyal companions Gladiolus, Ignis, and Prompto in the luxury convertible Regalia
Wields the Armiger ability, summoning spectral ancestral Royal Arms to warp-strike through space and deflect enemy blows
Sacrifices his own physical life inside the Crystal to banish the immortal daemon Ardyn Izunia and restore daylight to the world

facts_and_myths.claim: Noctis and his companions embarked on their journey solely as an open-world camping vacation before being surprised by the fall of Insomnia.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Noctis departed Insomnia under the official diplomatic mission to travel to the city of Altissia to marry Lady Lunafreya Nox Fleuret as part of an arranged peace treaty with the Niflheim Empire.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: King Regis knew the peace treaty was a deceitful imperial trap and deliberately sent Noctis away with his closest friends to ensure his survival.

facts_and_myths.claim: Noctis was originally conceived as the protagonist of Final Fantasy Versus XIII before the game underwent a ten-year development overhaul.
facts_and_myths.explanation: First unveiled at E3 2006 under director Tetsuya Nomura as Final Fantasy Versus XIII, the game lingered in development hell for years before being rebranded and reimagined as Final Fantasy XV in 2013.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Noctis retains several signature combat animations from the original Versus XIII CGI trailers, including telepathic weapon spinning.

name: Clive Rosfield
visual_anchor: Battle-hardened dark-haired warrior branded with an imperial bearer tattoo on his cheek, clad in crimson leather and steel armor, his right arm erupting into blazing volcanic hellfire as Ifrit flames surround him in vertical 9:16 framing.
core_traits: Firstborn prince of the Grand Duchy of Rosaria who was passed over by the Phoenix in favor of his frail younger brother Joshua
Sworn as the First Shield of Rosaria to protect his brother before tragedy at Phoenix Gate strips him of his noble status and enslaves him as a branded soldier
Discovers he is the Dominant of a second, impossible Eikon of Fire known as Ifrit, challenging centuries of Valisthean dogma
Absorbs the magical essences of multiple Eikons across Valisthea to destroy the Mothercrystals and liberate humanity from the deity Ultima

facts_and_myths.claim: Clive Rosfield was naturally born as a Bearer, explaining the magical enslavement tattoo branded on his left cheek.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Clive was born noble royalty without natural Bearer affliction; the imperial army of Sanbreque forcibly branded him as an enslaved Bearer after the fall of Rosaria to mask his royal identity and exploit his combat skills.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The brand is created with poisonous wyrm-venom ink that causes fatal necrosis if any enslaved person attempts to surgically remove it.

facts_and_myths.claim: Clive Rosfield's English voice actor, Ben Starr, based aspects of Clive's raw emotional grief on the real-life loss of his own father during recording.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Ben Starr channeled his authentic grief and vulnerability from his father's passing during the voice and performance capture sessions, delivering Clive's critically acclaimed heartfelt performance.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Ben Starr won the Golden Joystick Award for Best Lead Performer for his portrayal of Clive in 2023.

name: Squall Leonhart
visual_anchor: Stoic young military cadet with a sharp diagonal facial scar, black leather bomber jacket with white fur trim, aiming a revolving cylinder Gunblade forward with cold blue gaze inside a sterile high-tech garden academy in 9:16 vertical composition.
core_traits: Antisocial student at Balamb Garden military academy who trains rigorously to become an elite mercenary known as a SeeD
Master of the Gunblade, a hybrid weapon combining a razor-sharp sword edge with an integrated firing mechanism that triggers vibration shockwaves on impact
Bears a prominent diagonal scar across the bridge of his nose received during a fierce training duel against his rival Seifer Almasy
Overcomes his cynical emotional detachment to lead resistance forces against the time-compressing sorceress Ultimecia

facts_and_myths.claim: The famous Squall is Dead fan theory was officially confirmed by Final Fantasy VIII director Yoshinori Kitase as intended canon.
facts_and_myths.explanation: The popular theory claiming Squall died after being impaled by Edea's ice shard at the end of Disc 1 was explicitly debunked by Yoshinori Kitase, who clarified that Squall survived through magic and remained alive throughout the game.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Kitase admitted he found the fan theory fascinating and said he might consider integrating similar ideas if FFVIII were ever remade.

facts_and_myths.claim: Squall's Gunblade does not actually shoot bullets across long distances as projectiles during standard combat.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Gunblades in Final Fantasy VIII fire blank cartridges into the sword blade to create intense supersonic kinetic vibrations that maximize slashing damage, rather than firing bullets like a traditional gun.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Players can manually pull the controller's R1 trigger at the exact instant of impact to land guaranteed critical hits.

name: Dragonborn
visual_anchor: Nordic warrior clad in studded leather armor and an iconic horned iron helmet, holding an ancient steel sword and banded shield amidst a howling blizzard on the Throat of the World, throat glowing with Thu'um dragon power in vertical 9:16 view.
core_traits: Prophesied mortal born with the soul and blood of a dragon, blessed by the divine dragon god Akatosh
Possesses the innate ability to absorb the souls of slain dragons and instantly master powerful Shouts known as the Thu'um
Begins their journey as an anonymous captured prisoner narrowly escaping execution by the Imperial Legion at the ruined settlement of Helgen
Journeys into the realm of Sovngarde to defeat Alduin the World-Eater and prevent the destruction of the mortal world of Mundus

facts_and_myths.claim: The Last Dragonborn must canonically be a male Nord warrior as depicted in promotional artwork and official Skyrim trailers.
facts_and_myths.explanation: The Dragonborn's gender, race, appearance, morality, and combat specialization are entirely determined by the player, and Bethesda maintains all playable options as equally valid canon.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The iconic horned iron helmet and studded armor combo in trailers was chosen simply because it looked rugged, despite iron gear being among the weakest early-game armor.

facts_and_myths.claim: The Dragon Language created for the Dragonborn's Shouts was constructed as a functional 34-character rune script written with three claw marks and a dewclaw.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Bethesda designer Adam Adamowicz crafted the dragon alphabet using scratch-like wedge runes designed specifically so dragons could carve them into stone using three claws and a spur.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Every shout in Skyrim strictly adheres to a three-word meter, such as Fus-Ro-Dah, which translates to Force-Balance-Push.

name: Alduin
visual_anchor: Colossal black dragon with jagged volcanic obsidian scales and fiery crimson eyes roaring atop the misty celestial peaks of Sovngarde, summoning a cataclysmic meteor rain from the heavens, depicted in dramatic 9:16 vertical widescreen framing.
core_traits: Ancient and formidable black dragon regarded as the firstborn spawn of the divine god Akatosh in Tamrielic cosmology
Foresworn from his cosmic duty to end the current kalpa cycle, choosing instead to enslave humanity during the ancient Merethic Era Dragon Cult
Cast forward into the Fourth Era through the flow of time by ancient Nord tongues utilizing an Elder Scroll atop the Throat of the World
Devours the souls of the deceased inside Sovngarde to replenish his power before being defeated by the Last Dragonborn

facts_and_myths.claim: Alduin and Akatosh are identical names for the exact same deity worshipped identically across Skyrim and the Imperial province.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Although Imperial scholars often conflated them, the ancient Nords recognized Alduin as a distinct destructive deity who claims to be Akatosh's firstborn son, possessing an antithetical nature to Akatosh's role as the preserver of time.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Paarthurnax explicitly refers to Alduin as his older brother and confirms Alduin was the first creature spawned by Akatosh.

facts_and_myths.claim: Alduin cannot be permanently harmed or defeated by the Dragonborn without utilizing the Dragonrend shout to force him to experience mortality.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Being an immortal dragon unfamiliar with the concept of death, Alduin is completely invulnerable until hit by Dragonrend, which forces the incomprehensible concept of mortality into his mind and grounds him.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Ancient mortals created Dragonrend out of pure hatred and desperation, which is why Paarthurnax cannot teach it because dragons cannot truly conceive death.

name: Sheogorath
visual_anchor: Eccentric elderly nobleman with a manic grin and golden feline eyes, dressed in an extravagant split purple-and-amber regalia jacket, leaning leisurely upon the Wabbajack staff surrounded by flying cheese wheels in a whimsical 9:16 vertical portrait.
core_traits: Daedric Prince who presides over madness, insanity, creative delirium, and irrational obsession across the Aurbis
Rules the plane of Oblivion known as the Shivering Isles, divided into the colorful artistic realm of Mania and the paranoid dark realm of Dementia
Bestows upon adventurous mortals the legendary and unpredictable Wabbajack staff, which transmutes targets into random creatures or objects
Condemned by his fellow Daedric Princes to periodically transform into Jyggalag, the sterile and cold Prince of Order, in the Greymarch cycle

facts_and_myths.claim: Sheogorath was originally created by the universe as an inherently chaotic god of madness from the beginning of time.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Sheogorath was originally Jyggalag, the Daedric Prince of perfect Order; other Daedric Princes grew so terrified of Jyggalag's growing power that they cursed him to become his absolute antithesis: the Prince of Madness.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: At the end of each era, Jyggalag was allowed to reclaim his true form to wipe out the Shivering Isles before being forced back into madness.

facts_and_myths.claim: The Hero of Cyrodiil from The Elder Scrolls IV: Oblivion canonized mantle ascension by becoming the new Sheogorath.
facts_and_myths.explanation: In the Shivering Isles expansion, the player character defeats Jyggalag and breaks the Greymarch curse, mantling the divine station to rule the realm as the new Sheogorath, as referenced in Skyrim.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: When meeting Sheogorath in Skyrim's Pelagius wing, he cryptically reminisces about Martin Septim, butterfly wings, and severed heads from the Oblivion Crisis.

name: Commander Shepard
visual_anchor: Cinematic 9:16 vertical shot of Commander Shepard in battle-worn N7 carbon-fiber armor holding an omni-blade on the bridge of the SSV Normandy overlooking deep space and burning Reaper fleets.
core_traits: Decorated Systems Alliance naval officer who became the first human inducted into the elite Council Spectres
Commanding officer of the advanced stealth frigate SSV Normandy SR-1 and its Cerberus-rebuilt successor SR-2
Led a galaxy-spanning resistance across the Milky Way to unite disparate alien species against the apocalyptic Reaper invasion
Character actions and moral compass are shaped through the iconic binary morality system of Paragon or Renegade

facts_and_myths.claim: The character name Shepard was chosen as a tribute to Alan Shepard, the first American astronaut in space.
facts_and_myths.explanation: BioWare developers named Commander Shepard in honor of Alan Shepard, who made history in 1961 as the first American to travel into space aboard Freedom 7.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Male Shepard was voiced by Mark Meer while female Shepard was voiced by legendary voice actress Jennifer Hale.

facts_and_myths.claim: Commander Shepard was originally conceived exclusively as a male protagonist before BioWare added a female option late in development.
facts_and_myths.explanation: BioWare project director Casey Hudson confirmed that Shepard was envisioned with full gender parity from the inception of the Mass Effect franchise, with motion capture and voice acting planned equally for both.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Female Shepard became so universally beloved by fans that BioWare held an official fan vote to design her canonical appearance for the Mass Effect 3 cover art.

name: Garrus Vakarian
visual_anchor: Dramatic 9:16 vertical composition of turian sniper Garrus Vakarian in scarred blue-and-black C-Sec armor, aiming an anti-materiel sniper rifle through cracked visor glass in a gritty neon Omega alleyway.
core_traits: Former Citadel Security (C-Sec) investigator who grows frustrated with bureaucratic regulations and joins the Normandy crew
Skilled turian marksman and military tactician renowned for his sarcastic dry humor and unwavering loyalty to Commander Shepard
Operated under the vigilante alias Archangel on the lawless space station Omega, taking down criminal mercenary syndicates
Famous for spending his downtime constantly running diagnostics and calibrations on the Normandy's primary weapon batteries

facts_and_myths.claim: Garrus Vakarian was not an available romantic interest for female Shepard in the original Mass Effect game.
facts_and_myths.explanation: BioWare originally only included Liara and Kaidan as romances for female Shepard; overwhelming fan demand led writers to introduce Garrus as a full romance option in Mass Effect 2.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: His frequent line about needing to perform calibrations became BioWare's most celebrated running self-referential gag.

facts_and_myths.claim: Garrus is guaranteed to survive the Suicide Mission in Mass Effect 2 regardless of squad leader assignments.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Although Garrus is an ideal fireteam leader, choosing him for inappropriate roles or failing his loyalty mission can result in his permanent death before reaching Mass Effect 3.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: If loyal and given the fireteam leader assignment, Garrus performs flawlessly with zero squad casualties.

name: Liara T'Soni
visual_anchor: Ethereal 9:16 vertical portrait of Dr. Liara T'Soni summoning glowing blue biotic singularities around her hands amidst ancient Prothean ruins with holographic data glyphs floating in atmospheric dust.
core_traits: Asari maiden, archaeologist, and xenobiologist who dedicated over half a century to studying the extinct Prothean civilization
Powerful biotic adept who wields devastating singularities, warp fields, and stasis bubbles in combat
Infiltrated the base of the enigmatic information dealer and succeeded him to become the new galactic Shadow Broker
Daughter of Matriarch Benezia who plays a crucial role in discovering the Crucible superweapon schematics

facts_and_myths.claim: Liara was the one who recovered Commander Shepard's lifeless body from the Shadow Broker and delivered it to Cerberus for Project Lazarus.
facts_and_myths.explanation: In the canon Mass Effect: Redemption comic and game lore, Liara risked her life on Omega to prevent the Collectors from acquiring Shepard's body, handing it to Cerberus so Shepard could be revived.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Liara is one of only two squadmates present across the entirety of the original Mass Effect trilogy alongside Tali'Zorah.

facts_and_myths.claim: Liara was already considered a mature and elderly adult by asari cultural standards during the first Mass Effect.
facts_and_myths.explanation: At 106 years old, Liara is barely past adolescence for an asari, whose natural lifespans exceed one thousand years, making her an inexperienced maiden in their society.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Her youth is frequently pointed out by elder asari who dismiss her academic theories as youthful exuberance.

name: V
visual_anchor: Cyberpunk 9:16 vertical shot of mercenary V standing atop a rainy Night City rooftop, glowing yellow optics, Mantis Blades extended and drenched in neon pink reflections from towering holographic advertisements.
core_traits: Customizable mercenary protagonist operating out of Night City whose background stems from Nomad, Streetkid, or Corpo life paths
Partnered with Jackie Welles to pull off a daring high-stakes heist at Konpeki Plaza against the Arasaka Corporation
Survives an execution attempt only to wake up with an experimental Biochip stuck in their neural port
Races against terminal brain degradation caused by the digital engram of a deceased rockstar terrorist overwriting their consciousness

facts_and_myths.claim: The canonical full first name of V is Vincent for male voice tracks and Valerie for female voice tracks.
facts_and_myths.explanation: During specific intimate or vulnerable dialogue scenes in the campaign, dolls at Clouds and close confidants address V by their full given name: Vincent or Valerie.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: V insists that only close personal friends are allowed to call them by their real name instead of the single letter V.

facts_and_myths.claim: V's three life paths (Nomad, Streetkid, Corpo) branch into three completely different main storylines that never intersect.
facts_and_myths.explanation: The chosen life path provides a unique 30-minute prologue and specialized dialogue options, but all paths converge into the identical core narrative arc following the rescue of Sandra Dorsett.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Corpo V is the only starting path where the protagonist already personally knows Jackie Welles prior to the opening mission.

name: Johnny Silverhand
visual_anchor: Grungy 9:16 vertical action view of Johnny Silverhand wearing mirrored aviator sunglasses and leather vest, smoking a cigarette while brandishing his signature Malorian Arms pistol with gleaming chrome cybernetic left arm.
core_traits: Charismatic frontman and lead singer of the legendary anti-establishment chrome-rock band Samurai
Fierce anti-corporate insurgent who detonated a thermonuclear device inside Arasaka Tower during the Night City Holocaust of 2023
Possesses a cybernetic left cyberarm manufactured by Arasaka, earning him his famous rock moniker
Survives as a digitized consciousness stored on the Relic biochip trapped inside the brain of mercenary V

facts_and_myths.claim: Johnny Silverhand's physical appearance and voice acting were provided by Hollywood superstar Keanu Reeves.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Keanu Reeves performed extensive motion capture and voiced Johnny Silverhand, delivering thousands of lines of dialogue for both the base game and Phantom Liberty expansion.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Reeves enjoyed playing Johnny so much that he actively lobbied CD Projekt Red to expand his character's presence and screentime.

facts_and_myths.claim: Johnny Silverhand's playable flashback memories in Cyberpunk 2077 are completely objective, historically accurate accounts of the 2023 raid.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Tabletop creator Mike Pondsmith and in-game lore confirm Johnny is an unreliable narrator whose digitized memories were corrupted by radiation, ego, and Arasaka soul-killer manipulation.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: In original Cyberpunk tabletop lore, legendary solo Morgan Blackhand led the strike team that detonated the bomb, not Silverhand alone.

name: Malenia, Blade of Miquella
visual_anchor: High-drama 9:16 vertical composition of Malenia, Blade of Miquella hovering mid-air with radiant scarlet rot butterfly wings, unalloyed gold prosthetic arm raising a katana above blooming crimson flora in Elphael.
core_traits: Demigod daughter of Queen Marika and Radagon, born an Empyrean afflicted from birth with the devastating Scarlet Rot
Master swordswoman who wields a prosthetic unalloyed gold blade and never knew defeat in battle
Unleashed the Scarlet Aeonia bloom during the Shattering, transforming the lush region of Caelid into a poisoned wasteland
Famous for challenging players in Haligtree roots with her near-unavoidable flurry attack known as Waterfowl Dance

facts_and_myths.claim: Malenia's twin brother Miquella crafted needles out of unalloyed gold specifically to ward off the outer god of rot afflicting her.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Item lore confirms Miquella abandoned fundamentalist Golden Order incantations to develop unalloyed gold needles, which could stave off the meddling influence of outer gods and halt Malenia's rot.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: A legendary naked player named 'Let Me Solo Her' became an international gaming phenomenon by defeating Malenia thousands of times for struggling players.

facts_and_myths.claim: Malenia decisively killed General Radahn in battle during their climactic duel at the Battle of Aeonia.
facts_and_myths.explanation: The duel ended in a devastating stalemate; Malenia bloomed her scarlet rot which drove Radahn insane, but she fell unconscious and had to be carried back to the Haligtree by Cleanrot Knight Finlay.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Finlay carried the comatose Malenia across the entire continent of the Lands Between to safety.

versus_candidates: Lady Maria of the Astral Clocktower

name: Ranni the Witch
visual_anchor: Mystical 9:16 vertical portrait of four-armed Ranni the Witch in oversized pointed white snow witch hat and fur cloak, glowing spectral ethereal face shimmering beside her porcelain doll visage under a crescent moon.
core_traits: Empyrean daughter of Radagon and Rennala who orchestrated the Night of the Black Knives to slay her own Empyrean flesh
Inhabits a four-armed porcelain doll modeled after the secret Snow Witch who taught her cold lunar sorcery
Rejects the Greater Will and the Golden Order to usher in the quiet, star-guided thousand-year Age of the Stars
Bound by fate to the movement of the celestial stars, which remain frozen until the defeat of General Radahn
distractor_pool: Rennala, Queen of the Full Moon

facts_and_myths.claim: Ranni stole a fragment of the Rune of Death from Maliketh to forge the daggers used to assassinate Godwyn the Golden.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Ranni infused Black Knife assassins' blades with the stolen Rune of Death, executing a dark ritual where Godwyn died in soul while Ranni's physical body died in flesh simultaneously.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Players who follow Ranni's extensive questline can offer her the Dark Moon Ring to trigger one of the game's major unique endings.

facts_and_myths.claim: The doll body Ranni inhabits was sculpted to represent her true original biological appearance before the Night of the Black Knives.
facts_and_myths.explanation: In-game lore reveals her doll body was deliberately modeled after her secret childhood mentor, the old Snow Witch, while Ranni's original biological corpse atop the Divine Tower of Liurnia had red hair.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Ranni's original charred body atop the Divine Tower reveals she was once exceptionally tall like her father Radagon.

name: Radahn
visual_anchor: Imposing 9:16 vertical perspective of colossal General Radahn wielding dual colossal curved greatswords, lion-crested golden helmet with billowing red mane, riding his undersized scrawny steed Leonard on crimson sands.
core_traits: Mighty demigod general and son of Radagon and Rennala, famed as the fiercest warrior of the Shattering
Mastered gravitational magic in the town of Sellia so he could continue riding his beloved scrawny warhorse Leonard
Conquered the cosmos in his youth by single-handedly halting the movement of constellations and falling star beasts
Driven mad by Scarlet Rot after clashing with Malenia, leading to the grand Radahn Festival at Redmane Castle

facts_and_myths.claim: Radahn continuously uses gravitational magic during combat to make himself completely weightless so he does not crush his horse.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Item descriptions confirm Radahn was so deeply attached to his scrawny childhood horse Leonard that he studied gravity magic specifically to lighten his immense bulk.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Even while driven totally feral by scarlet rot, his instinctual love for Leonard kept him sustaining the anti-gravity spell.

facts_and_myths.claim: Radahn lost his sanity due to the direct corrupting power of the Elden Ring's Great Runes.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Radahn's mental degradation was caused strictly by Malenia blooming the toxic Scarlet Aeonia into his neck during the battle of Caelid, rotting his mind while his body remained alive.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: During his boss fight, Radahn launches himself thousands of feet into the stratosphere before plummeting back down as a burning meteor.

name: The Tarnished
visual_anchor: Atmospheric 9:16 vertical composition of The Tarnished in battered Raging Wolf armor leaning on a glowing broadsword while resting beside a golden Site of Grace beneath the colossal radiant Erdtree.
core_traits: Descendant of the exiled warriors stripped of grace by Queen Marika following Godfrey's Long March
Summoned back to the Lands Between by the rekindled Guidance of Grace following the cataclysmic Shattering
Aided by the spectral steed Torrent and the mysterious finger maiden Melina to convert runes into martial power
Fated to defeat demigod shardbearers, mend or reshape the shattered Elden Ring, and ascend as Elden Lord

facts_and_myths.claim: The first Tarnished were formerly Godfrey's warriors who had the golden hue taken from their eyes when Marika banished them.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Lore spoken by Melina at Church ruins states Queen Marika divested Godfrey and his army of their Grace, sending them to fight and die in distant lands so they would grow stronger upon resurrection.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Godfrey himself became the very first Tarnished under the mortal identity of Hoarah Loux, Chieftain of the Badlands.

facts_and_myths.claim: All Tarnished in the Lands Between can still see the golden guidance of Grace leading them toward the Erdtree.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Dialogue with NPCs like Corhyn and Rogier confirms most Tarnished lost the ability to perceive Grace long ago, making the player character exceptionally rare for still following its golden trails.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Rogier expresses solemn melancholy that the golden beams visible to the player are completely invisible to him.

name: Artorias the Abysswalker
visual_anchor: Haunting 9:16 vertical view of Knight Artorias in corrupted silver armor with ragged blue cloth, one crippled arm dangling uselessly as he swings his massive greatsword radiating black Abyss slime in Oolacile.
core_traits: One of the Four Knights of Lord Gwyn, renowned for his unbending steel will and unmatched greatsword proficiency
Formed a covenant with the beasts of the Abyss to travel into the void and stop the spread of darkness in Oolacile
Sacrificed his greatshield to cast a protective barrier that safeguarded his companion wolf puppy Sif
Overwhelmed by Manus, Father of the Abyss, leaving him a corrupted hollow husk fighting on feral warrior instinct

facts_and_myths.claim: Artorias's left arm was shattered and completely broken when players face him in the Colosseum of Oolacile.
facts_and_myths.explanation: When Artorias shielded Sif from the Abyss, his shield arm was maimed, forcing him to fight the Chosen Undead using only his right arm while his broken left arm hangs limp.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Despite fighting with his off-hand and a broken arm, Artorias remains one of the most acrobatic and lethal bosses in Dark Souls.

facts_and_myths.claim: Artorias successfully vanquished Manus and halted the spread of the dark Abyss in ancient Oolacile.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Artorias was defeated and corrupted by Manus; it was actually the time-traveling Chosen Undead who slew Manus, while history falsely attributed the heroic victory to Artorias.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Elizabeth the mushroom matriarch promises to keep the secret and preserve Artorias's honorable legacy for posterity.

name: Solaire of Astora
visual_anchor: Cinematic 9:16 vertical portrait of Solaire of Astora in chainmail armor and painted white surcoat emblazoned with a beaming radiant sun, arms raised high in the iconic Praise the Sun gesture against an ethereal golden Lordran sky.
core_traits: Devout warrior hailing from Astora who voluntarily chose undead status to travel across Lordran in search of his own personal sun
Founder and figurehead of the Warriors of Sunlight covenant who offers jolly cooperation to adventurers tackling grueling trials
Wields a standard iron round shield, straight sword, and hurled lightning spears channeled through profound spiritual devotion
Immortalized among gaming lore for greeting travelers with arms held high toward the heavens while uttering Praise the Sun

facts_and_myths.claim: Solaire is not an ancient deity or royal bloodline, but an ordinary warrior who achieved heroic status purely through intense mortal devotion and training.
facts_and_myths.explanation: In Dark Souls design interviews, creator Hidetaka Miyazaki confirmed that Solaire possessed no divine lineage, and all his equipment bears descriptions noting it was mundane gear made exceptional solely by his sheer will.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: His distinctive sun emblem on his chest tunic is hand-painted by Solaire himself rather than being an official kingdom heraldry.

facts_and_myths.claim: Solaire is the secret firstborn god of Lord Gwyn who was stripped of his deific status and cast out from Anor Londo.
facts_and_myths.explanation: This was one of the most famous community theories during Dark Souls 1, but Dark Souls 3 formally disproved it by introducing the Nameless King as Gwyn's true exiled eldest son.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Miyazaki admitted he loved the fan theory so much that it shaped how he approached the lore of the Nameless King in later installments.

name: Gwyn, Lord of Cinder
visual_anchor: Dramatic 9:16 vertical composition of Gwyn, Lord of Cinder, wielding a massive flaming greatsword amid ash mounds in the Kiln of the First Flame, white beard flowing beneath a golden crown as melancholy piano notes echo.
core_traits: Supreme deity of Lordran who led the ancient war against the Everlasting Dragons using lightning bolts stripped from the sky
Discovered a Light Soul within the First Flame and established the gilded divine capital of Anor Londo during the Age of Fire
Sacrificed his own divine body and soul to link the fading First Flame, transforming into a burned, hollowed shell guarding the Kiln
Final boss of Dark Souls renowned for fighting without dialogue, accompanied only by a poignant, melancholic three-note piano theme

facts_and_myths.claim: The final battle soundtrack against Gwyn is performed on a piano played strictly with white keys to emphasize sorrow over malice.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Composer Motoi Sakuraba deliberately scored Gwyn's theme, 'Gwyn, Lord of Cinder', using only natural piano keys without black sharp or flat keys, creating a somber lament rather than an aggressive victory anthem.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Gwyn is susceptible to parrying, making one of the most feared gods in gaming history surprisingly counterable with basic parry timing.

facts_and_myths.claim: Gwyn prolonged the Age of Fire purely as an act of noble benevolence to save human mortals from doom.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Gwyn feared humanity and the power of the Dark Soul, imposing the Darksign curse upon mankind to bind humanity's true strength and preserve his divine hierarchy.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The Ringed City expansion in Dark Souls 3 revealed that Gwyn gifted a city to early humans specifically to exile and monitor them.

name: Hunter
visual_anchor: Atmospheric vertical 9:16 portrait of the Hunter clad in a worn leather tricorn hat and heavy duster coat, holding a transformed Saw Cleaver and Hunter Pistol amid cobblestone Yharnam streets under a blood-red moon.
core_traits: Outsider who travels to the plague-ridden Victorian gothic city of Yharnam seeking miraculous medicinal blood transfusion to cure an affliction
Tethered to the mystical Hunter's Dream sanctuary, granting resurrection and guidance under the tutelage of Gehrman and the Plain Doll
Employs high-speed aggressive gun-parrying and trick weapons that switch mechanical forms mid-combo to harvest beastly blood
Hunts through the Long Night under the Paleblood lunar eclipse, transcending mortal humanity to confront eldritch Great Ones

facts_and_myths.claim: The Rally mechanic was explicitly engineered by FromSoftware to force players to abandon defensive shield turtling in favor of frenetic counter-attacks.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Director Hidetaka Miyazaki intentionally removed standard shields from Bloodborne and implemented Rally so players immediately regenerate lost health by striking enemies back within a tight window.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The only wooden shield available in Yharnam includes an in-game item description that outright mocks defensive playstyles.

facts_and_myths.claim: The Hunter is confirmed to be a native-born Yharnamite noble who betrayed the Healing Church.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Every opening narrative dialogue and clinic document emphasizes that the protagonist is an outsider from a distant foreign land who arrived solely to receive blood therapy.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Consuming three pieces of Third Umbilical Cord allows the Hunter to reject Flora and ascend into an infant Great One in the secret ending.

name: Lady Maria of the Astral Clocktower
visual_anchor: Striking 9:16 vertical composition of Lady Maria seated lifeless on a high-backed velvet chair beneath a grand luminous clocktower dial, dual Rakuyo blades ready to ignite with crimson blood and searing hellfire.
core_traits: Distant blood relative of Queen Annalise of Cainhurst who renounced blood blades and studied hunting directly under First Hunter Gehrman
Guards the luminal gate leading to the Fishing Hamlet inside the Hunter's Nightmare to keep the atrocities of Byrgenwerth concealed
Dual-wields the twin Rakuyo curved sword and dagger, escalating her battle through three phases combining blood magic and explosive pyromancy
Served as the physical muse and anatomical model upon which Gehrman sculpted the enigmatic, porcelain Plain Doll

facts_and_myths.claim: The Plain Doll in the Hunter's Dream shares both the voice actress and exact facial bone structure of Lady Maria.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Voice actress Evetta Muradasilova voiced both characters, and in-game model rips confirm their facial meshes are virtually identical, confirming Gehrman modeled the Doll on Maria.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: After defeating Maria in The Old Hunters expansion, visiting the Doll triggers special dialogue where the Doll feels an inexplicable sense of liberated peace.

facts_and_myths.claim: Lady Maria used blood arts throughout her entire hunting career as a member of the Healing Church.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Lore descriptions note that Maria despised her Cainhurst bloodline arts and only wielded pure dexterous swordplay until overwhelming desperation in her boss fight forced her to unleash blood and fire.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Maria discarded her beloved sword Rakuyo into a dark well in the Fishing Hamlet after growing disgusted by the slaughter of the local villagers.

name: Wolf
visual_anchor: Dynamic vertical 9:16 framing of Wolf perched silently on a snowy pagoda roof in feudal Sengoku Japan, Kusabimaru katana unsheathed and shinobi prosthetic arm equipped with an iron grappling hook.
core_traits: Stoic shinobi bound by the Iron Code to protect his young master, Divine Heir Kuro, through Sengoku-era Ashina
Rebuilt by the Sculptor with a versatile wooden and iron mechanical prosthetic arm fitted with tools like shurikens and firecrackers
Possesses the Dragon's Heritage resurrective resurrection blessing, allowing him to defy death on the battlefield at the cost of spreading Dragonrot
Specializes in relentless posture deflection swordplay, mikiri counters, and lethal deathblow executions with his katana Kusabimaru

facts_and_myths.claim: The moniker 'Sekiro' given to Wolf by Lord Isshin Ashina is a compound abbreviation meaning 'One-Armed Wolf'.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Isshin coins the name Sekiro by combining 'seki' (one/single/severed) and 'ro' (wolf), describing his missing arm and predatory demeanor.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Wolf was originally found as a starving orphan scavenger wandering a war-torn battlefield by the Owl, who tested the boy by slashing his cheek.

facts_and_myths.claim: Sekiro was originally conceptualized as an open-world sequel to Bloodborne.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Sekiro originated when FromSoftware set out to make a new game inspired by the classic stealth-action franchise Tenchu before evolving into a unique standalone IP.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: FromSoftware originally owned rights to the Tenchu series, and early prototypes were explicitly pitched as a modern Tenchu reimagining.

name: Isshin, the Sword Saint
visual_anchor: Breathtaking 9:16 vertical action view of Isshin, the Sword Saint, standing in silver grass beneath stormy skies, brandishing a massive cross-spear and katana crackling with redirected lightning alongside a concealed semi-automatic pistol.
core_traits: Legendary warlord who forged the rebellious nation of Ashina through bloody coup d'etat and peerless mastery of martial arts
Known as an eccentric elder who prowled the rooftops disguised as the Tengu mask vigilante to hunt interior ministry rats
Summoned back from the underworld in his youthful physical prime through the sacrificial Black Mortal Blade by Genichiro
Famous for challenging Wolf with a katana, giant yari spear, sweeping lightning attacks, and an infamous rapid-fire Glock firearm

facts_and_myths.claim: Isshin's combat philosophy dictates that true winning in battle requires utilizing any viable weapon or tactic rather than adhering to rigid honor.
facts_and_myths.explanation: In Ashina style lore, Isshin expressly states that the core dogma of Ashina esoteric arts is to do whatever it takes to win, justifying his use of pistols, spears, and lightning.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: His dying words in combat, 'Hesitation is defeat', became one of the most widespread catchphrases and memes across modern gaming.

facts_and_myths.claim: Isshin returned from the dead because he passionately desired immortal power and wanted to seize the Dragon's Heritage.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Isshin despised immortality and opposed Genichiro's obsession with it; he fought Sekiro upon resurrection solely because the Black Mortal Blade bound him to honor his grandson's dying wish.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Throughout the story before his death from old age, Isshin actively aids Wolf by offering sake, lore wisdom, and combat techniques.

name: Sora
visual_anchor: Vibrant 9:16 vertical portrait of Sora with spiky brown hair, oversized yellow shoes, and silver crown necklace, triumphantly pointing the gleaming Kingdom Key Keyblade upward toward a heart-shaped moon.
core_traits: Upbeat, kindhearted youth from Destiny Islands whose heart was chosen to wield the mystical Kingdom Key weapon
Journeys through iconic Disney and Square Enix realms aboard the Gummi Ship accompanied by Donald Duck and Goofy
Battles the shadow Heartless, Organization XIII Nobodies, and the dark machinations of Master Xehanort across timelines
Draws unstoppable strength from unbreakable friendship bonds, declaring that his friends are his true power

facts_and_myths.claim: Sora was originally conceptualized as a half-human, half-lion hybrid wielding a massive chainsaw-like blade.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Early concept art by Tetsuya Nomura featured an anthropomorphic lion boy with a chain blade before Disney executives and Square Enix opted for a human protagonist wielding a magical Keyblade.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Sora was the final DLC fighter officially added to the crossover fighting game Super Smash Bros. Ultimate following an unprecedented worldwide fan vote.

facts_and_myths.claim: The Kingdom Key Keyblade was forged specifically and exclusively for Sora from the day he was born.
facts_and_myths.explanation: The Kingdom Key originally manifested on Destiny Islands to choose Riku, but Riku's heart briefly fell into darkness, leading the Keyblade to choose Sora instead.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Sora's name is derived from the Japanese word for 'sky', fittingly contrasting with Riku ('land') and Kairi ('sea').

name: Riku
visual_anchor: Cool-toned 9:16 vertical framing of Riku featuring silver hair and piercing blue-green eyes, wielding the dark Soul Eater sword transitioning into the Braveheart Keyblade while walking between twilight shadows.
core_traits: Silver-haired prodigy from Destiny Islands who longed to explore outer worlds beyond the ocean horizon
Fell into the corrupting sway of Maleficent and Ansem, temporarily losing himself to darkness before fighting to redeem his soul
Walks the intermediate Path of Twilight and Road to Dawn, mastering both light and dark energies in perfect equilibrium
Officially passes the Mark of Mastery exam before Sora to become a certified, recognized Keyblade Master

facts_and_myths.claim: Riku was chosen as the original rightful heir to the Kingdom Key through the Keyblade inheritance ceremony performed by Terra.
facts_and_myths.explanation: During Birth by Sleep, Keyblade Master Terra performed the Bequeathing rite with young Riku, selecting him as the future wielder before Riku's temporary fall to darkness.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Riku blinded himself with a blindfold during Kingdom Hearts 358/2 Days because his inner dark eyes couldn't bear to lie about his true identity.

facts_and_myths.claim: Riku permanently purged all darkness from his heart after defeating Ansem, Seeker of Darkness.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Rather than obliterating his dark power, Riku learned to accept, tame, and channel darkness harmoniously alongside light, making him unique among Keyblade Masters.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Riku's iconic intermediate blade, Way to the Dawn, manifests from his transformed soul weapon, Soul Eater.

name: Chrono
visual_anchor: Nostalgic 9:16 vertical anime-style rendering of Chrono with spiky crimson red hair and yellow headband, poised with a gleaming katana charged with crackling Luminaire lightning sparks in front of the Epoch time machine.
core_traits: Spiky red-haired silent swordsman from the peaceful village of Truce who stumbles into time travel at the Millennial Fair
Journeys across prehistoric, medieval, post-apocalyptic, and magical antique eras aboard the flying time-ship Epoch
Wields deadly katana techniques infused with elemental lightning magic, climaxing in the legendary spell Luminaire
Unites diverse allies across millennia including a robotic humanoid, prehistoric chieftain, medieval knight frog, and reformed sorcerer

facts_and_myths.claim: Chrono can be permanently left dead for the remainder of the game if players choose not to revive him atop Death Peak.
facts_and_myths.explanation: After Chrono sacrifices himself against Lavos in the Ocean Palace, completing the quest with the Chrono Trigger doll to resurrect him is entirely optional to finish the game.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Chrono character designer Akira Toriyama styled Chrono's iconic spiked hair and determined face very similarly to his Dragon Ball protagonist Goku.

facts_and_myths.claim: Chrono was given multiple spoken dialogue lines in the original unreleased Japanese Super Famicom version.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Chrono was always designed as a strictly silent protagonist so players could project themselves directly into his shoes, speaking only in a single humorous alternate ending.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: His canonical English spelling in the SNES cartridge was shortened to 'Crono' due to a strict five-character name limit in the menu system.

name: 2B
visual_anchor: Cinematic 9:16 vertical composition of 2B in her elegant black gothic dress and blindfold visor, floating white hair framing her porcelain face as she wields Virtuous Treaty over a ruined overgrown city.
core_traits: All-purpose battle android deployed by the lunar YoRHa military council to reclaim post-apocalyptic Earth from alien machine lifeforms
Outfitted with a sleek gothic lolita combat dress, black optical visor blindfold, and supported by aerial tactical Pod 042
Executes acrobatic dual-weapon martial arts using floating katanas and heavy greatswords like Virtuous Contract and Virtuous Treaty
Harbors a tragic classified secret mission as an Executioner model tasked with repeatedly assassinating her inquisitive partner 9S

facts_and_myths.claim: Her designated designation '2B' is a deliberate cover identity concealing her true classification as executioner android '2E'.
facts_and_myths.explanation: YoRHa Command classified her as an E-type (Executioner) model stationed to monitor scanner unit 9S and execute him whenever he discovered the truth about humanity's extinction.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Her trademark blindfold is not an eye patch but a high-tech tactical HUD visor projecting combat telemetry directly onto her sensors.

facts_and_myths.claim: 2B is an emotionless machine who experiences no genuine empathy or grief toward 9S during their operations.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Despite reciting the YoRHa military mantra 'emotions are prohibited', 2B experiences immense internal sorrow and heartbreak every time she is forced to reset 9S's memories.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Creator Yoko Taro jokingly stated that the primary reason 2B wears high heels in battle is simply because he likes girls in high heels.

name: Steve
visual_anchor: Cinematic vertical 9:16 portrait of Steve in his classic light blue short-sleeved shirt and indigo jeans, wielding an enchanted glowing purple diamond pickaxe inside a deep stone cave lit by flickering torches and molten orange lava.
core_traits: Default masculine player avatar of Mojang's iconic sandbox world, introduced during early development by Markus Persson.
Capable of punching through trees with bare hands, mining solid rock, and crafting elaborate contraptions from raw materials.
Possesses extraordinary physical strength in gameplay lore, able to carry thousands of cubic meters of solid gold blocks in his inventory.
Famous for his blocky pixelated appearance, bright cyan tee, dark blue trousers, and signature goatee-style smile.

facts_and_myths.claim: Steve was named somewhat jokingly by creator Notch before becoming the official canonical name of the character.
facts_and_myths.explanation: When asked about the protagonist's name during early Minecraft development, Markus 'Notch' Persson casually suggested 'Steve?' as a placeholder joke, which fans embraced until it became officially canonized.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Steve was added as a playable fighter in Super Smash Bros. Ultimate in 2020, requiring Nintendo to rework every stage to accommodate his block-placing mechanic.

facts_and_myths.claim: The dark pixel shape on the lower half of classic Steve's face was originally designed to represent an open smiling mouth.
facts_and_myths.explanation: The dark pixels were intended to be a stubble beard or goatee, but because many players interpreted it as a wide toothy grin, Mojang removed it in updated default textures before later restoring it.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Steve's original hurt sound effect in the alpha versions of Minecraft was an infamous human grunt recorded directly by Notch.

name: Alex
visual_anchor: Dynamic vertical 9:16 composition of Alex standing atop an overgrown jungle temple at sunrise, sporting long orange hair tied in a ponytail, green tunic, brown boots, and drawing a loaded crossbow with glowing spectral arrows.
core_traits: Second default player avatar introduced to Minecraft in update 1.8 to bring character diversity and a slimmer model option.
Recognizable by long ginger hair draped over one shoulder, bright green eyes, a pale green tunic, and three-pixel-wide arms.
Shares identical survival and crafting capabilities with Steve, mastering alchemy, archery, redstone engineering, and Nether exploration.
Features a narrower arm model that became the standard base template for customized slim player skins across the community.

facts_and_myths.claim: Alex was introduced to the game with narrower character arms measuring three pixels wide instead of Steve's four.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Mojang designed Alex with the 'slim' model framework featuring 3-pixel-wide arms to give players a choice between classic bulky proportions and a lighter build.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Her default physical appearance was widely inspired by Mojang employee and lead developer Jens 'Jeb' Bergensten.

facts_and_myths.claim: Alex was created with faster running speed and lower hit points than Steve to distinguish their combat playstyles.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Steve and Alex have completely identical hit points, movement speed, inventory capacity, and gameplay mechanics, differing solely in cosmetic visual models.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: When first implemented in 2014, players without custom skins were randomly assigned either Steve or Alex based on their unique account ID.

name: Creeper
visual_anchor: Tense vertical 9:16 night shot of a mottled green Creeper creeping stealthily through tall oak forest grass, its four stubby clawed feet stepping silently while dark hollow eyes and mouth begin to flash white with impending detonation.
core_traits: Stealthy hostile mob that approaches players silently before hissing loudly and self-destructing.
Born from a famous coding mistake by Notch when he accidentally inverted the height and length values of a pig model.
Characterized by a pixelated green camouflage texture, four short walking legs, and a frowning square visage.
Transforms into an electrified charged variant with massively amplified explosive force when struck by lightning.

facts_and_myths.claim: The Creeper model was accidentally created while Notch was attempting to code the model for a pig.
facts_and_myths.explanation: While programming a pig model in 2009, Markus Persson swapped the height and length coordinate variables, creating a bizarre tall creature with four stubby legs that he kept and re-textured into the Creeper.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Creepers are terrified of ocelots and domestic cats, immediately fleeing whenever a feline is nearby.

facts_and_myths.claim: Creepers drop music discs whenever they successfully kill a player with their suicide blast.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Creepers drop music discs only when their final fatal blow is delivered by a skeleton or stray's arrow, not when they kill players.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The Creeper face has become the iconic brand logo of Minecraft, appearing integrated directly into the letter 'A' of the title.

name: Ender Dragon
visual_anchor: Dramatic vertical 9:16 low-angle perspective of the massive Ender Dragon circling high above dark obsidian pillars in the void, glowing purple eyes glaring as she spews harmful dragon breath down upon floating end stone islands.
core_traits: The first official boss mob added to Minecraft, guarding the desolate void dimension known as The End.
Heals continuously from beam-emitting end crystals perched atop towering obsidian pillars.
Upon defeat, drops immense amounts of experience, generates an exit portal back to the Overworld, and displays the poetic End Poem credits.
Officially nicknamed 'Jean?' by Notch in response to community questions regarding the dragon's true identity.

facts_and_myths.claim: The Ender Dragon is canonically female and lays a single unobtainable dragon egg atop the exit portal upon her first defeat.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Notch confirmed the dragon is a female named Jean, proven in-game by the manifestation of the Dragon Egg trophy block on the central bedrock pedestal after she is slain.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Players can re-summon the Ender Dragon as many times as they want by placing four end crystals around the borders of the exit portal.

facts_and_myths.claim: Hatching the dragon egg in the Overworld allows players to tame and ride a baby Ender Dragon.
facts_and_myths.explanation: In vanilla Minecraft, the dragon egg is strictly a decorative trophy block that cannot be hatched into a companion without third-party modifications.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Beds placed in the End dimension explode with greater force than TNT, making them a popular speedrunning tactic to slay the Ender Dragon quickly.

name: Sans
visual_anchor: Atmospheric vertical 9:16 shot of Sans standing in the sunlit Judgement Hall, hands casually tucked into blue hoodie pockets, left eye socket igniting with flashing cyan and yellow flame while skeletal Gaster Blasters loom in the background.
core_traits: Laid-back, pun-loving skeleton sentry in Snowdin who frequently slacks off at hot dog stands and pranks the protagonist.
Serves as the notoriously unforgiving final boss in the Genocide route, punishing players for their sins in the Last Corridor.
Attacks with telekinesis, bone mazes, and laser-firing dragon-like skulls known as Gaster Blasters while breaking fourth-wall mechanics.
Named after the Comic Sans typeface, which he uses exclusively for all of his dialogue text boxes.

facts_and_myths.claim: Sans only deals one point of base damage per hit, but bypasses invulnerability frames using a draining status effect called Karma.
facts_and_myths.explanation: In his boss fight, Sans's attacks have an attack stat of 1, but they deal damage continuously on every single frame of contact while inflicting KR poison damage.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Sans is the only enemy in Undertale who actively dodges the player's physical attacks instead of enduring the damage.

facts_and_myths.claim: Sans is confirmed by Toby Fox to be the human character Ness from EarthBound in a secret alternate timeline.
facts_and_myths.explanation: The theory that Sans is Ness was an entertaining viral internet hypothesis popularized by Game Theory, but it has never been canonical lore in Toby Fox's universe.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Sans's iconic battle theme 'Megalovania' was originally composed by Toby Fox for an EarthBound Halloween Hack and later used in Homestuck before Undertale.

name: Papyrus
visual_anchor: Vibrant 9:16 vertical portrait of Papyrus striking a flamboyant heroic pose in snowy woods, wearing his handmade battle body armor, flowing red cape, and bright red boots while proudly holding up a steaming plate of spaghetti.
core_traits: Flamboyant, loud, and kindhearted skeleton living in Snowdin who passionately dreams of joining the elite Royal Guard.
Crafts elaborate yet comically harmless puzzle traps and has a bizarre obsession with cooking spaghetti that he rarely eats.
Speaks in ALL CAPS using the Papyrus font and refers to himself proudly in the third person as 'The Great Papyrus'.
His boss battle features the 'blue soul' gravity mechanic, yet he is so compassionate that he refuses to kill the player, capturing them instead.

facts_and_myths.claim: Papyrus cannot actually kill the player during his boss battle, leaving them at 1 HP and imprisoning them in his doghouse.
facts_and_myths.explanation: If Papyrus's attacks reduce the player's HP to 1, the battle peacefully ends, and the human is safely placed inside his unlocked garage with a bowl of dog food.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Papyrus's online username in the UnderNet forum is 'CoolSkeleton95', hinting at his youthful, exuberant personality.

facts_and_myths.claim: Spaghetti is Papyrus's favorite food to eat for breakfast, lunch, and dinner.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Toby Fox revealed in an official Q&A that Papyrus has never actually eaten his own spaghetti because he just likes cooking it; his real favorite food is dinosaur egg oatmeal.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Papyrus created his distinctive 'battle body' costume for a costume party a few weeks prior to the game and simply never took it off.

name: The Knight
visual_anchor: Moody vertical 9:16 illustration of The Knight standing on a damp blue bench in the City of Tears, clutching their bone-white Old Nail while rain cascades down weathered limestone architecture illuminated by glowing lumafly lanterns.
core_traits: Silent, genderless Vessel crafted from the God of Hallownest and Void, born in the Abyss to contain the infection.
Wields a signature bladed nail, absorbing Soul from strikes to mend wounds or cast destructive spells like Vengeful Spirit.
Features a stark white horned shell-mask, dark shroud-like cloak, and hollow black eye sockets containing nothingness.
Descends into the ruined insect kingdom of Hallownest to break the Dreamer seals and confront the Radiance.

facts_and_myths.claim: The Knight is not the titular 'Hollow Knight' referenced in the game's title, but rather an abandoned sibling.
facts_and_myths.explanation: The actual titular Hollow Knight is the fully grown Vessel chosen by the Pale King and sealed inside the Black Egg Temple, while the player character is an escaped discard.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Hornet and the White Lady frequently refer to The Knight affectionately as 'Ghost' or 'Little Ghost'.

facts_and_myths.claim: The Knight is biologically male and possesses a defined personality revealed through internal monologue.
facts_and_myths.explanation: As a Vessel forged from the Void, The Knight is completely genderless, has no voice to cry suffering, and never speaks or expresses an internal monologue throughout the adventure.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: When The Knight dies, they leave behind a hostile Shade made of pure Void that must be defeated to recover lost Geo.

name: Hornet
visual_anchor: Dynamic vertical 9:16 framing of Hornet leaping gracefully through the misty greenery of Greenpath, crimson cloaks billowing around her needle weapon tethered to glistening white silk threads as she prepares a mid-air dash.
core_traits: Fierce protector of Hallownest's ruins who tests the strength of Vessels with her rapid needle-and-thread combat.
