Daughter of the Pale King and Herrah the Beast, earning her the title of gendered child among the genderless vessels.
Recognizable by her flowing scarlet cloak, curved two-pronged white mask, and sharp needle weapon.
Stars as the agile, silk-weaving protagonist of the highly anticipated sequel Hollow Knight: Silksong.

facts_and_myths.claim: Unlike The Knight and other Vessels, Hornet was not born of Void and is not genderless.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Hornet was conceived through a pact between the Pale King and Herrah the Beast, making her a biological spider-wyrm hybrid rather than a void-infused vessel.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Hornet's famous battle cry often sounds to players like 'Shaw!' and 'Git Gud!', which became widespread gaming memes.

facts_and_myths.claim: Hornet was originally designed from the beginning to be an insectoid wasp or bee based on her name.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Team Cherry named her Hornet because she is fierce and quick like a hornet, but her parentage from Deepnest makes her part spider (weaver) rather than a flying wasp.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Silksong was initially planned as a Kickstarter stretch-goal DLC before expanding into a full standalone sequel due to the scope of Hornet's abilities.

name: Zagreus
visual_anchor: Epic vertical 9:16 shot of Zagreus dashing across the fiery floor of Asphodel, flaming feet leaving scorching footprints while wielding the Stygian Blade wreathed in Olympic boons of golden divine lightning and sea spray.
core_traits: Charming and persistent Prince of the Underworld determined to battle through Tartarus, Asphodel, and Elysium to reach the surface.
Son of the God of the Dead who seeks to find his biological mother, Persephone, with help from his Olympian relatives.
Features heterochromia with one red and one green eye, glowing red blood, and feet permanently wreathed in laurel flames.
Wields the six Infernal Arms, including the Stygian Blade and Coronacht, adapting them with god boons across repeated escape runs.

facts_and_myths.claim: Zagreus cannot survive long on the surface of Greece due to a divine binding tied to the Underworld.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Whenever Zagreus successfully escapes to the mortal surface, the Fates ensure his life force swiftly fails, returning him via the river Styx back to the House of Hades.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Zagreus has a special interaction with Cerberus where he can stop to pet all three of the giant hound's heads between escape attempts.

facts_and_myths.claim: Zagreus was completely invented by Supergiant Games as an original protagonist with no basis in ancient mythology.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Zagreus is an obscure ancient Greek mythological figure connected to Orphism, often considered an early underworld deity or prototype of Dionysus.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: In the game, Zagreus and Dionysus play a prank on Orpheus by feeding him ridiculous fabricated myths about their shared identity.

name: Hades
visual_anchor: Towering 9:16 vertical composition of Lord Hades seated upon his massive obsidian throne in the House of Hades, draped in luxurious crimson robes, glowing golden jewelry, and holding a giant bident while reviewing Underworld scrolls.
core_traits: Stern, overworked ruler of the Underworld who manages the endless bureaucracy of the realm of the dead.
Father of Zagreus who serves as the final boss awaiting the prince on the snow-covered surface at the gateway to Greece.
Wields the massive spear Gigaros, summons darkness and boiling blood, and commands urn traps during his two-phase boss encounter.
Deeply bitter toward his Olympian brothers Zeus and Poseidon for abandoning him to manage the grim subterranean underworld.

facts_and_myths.claim: Hades has a secret Extreme Measures phase in the Pact of Punishment that reveals a third combat phase with Cerberus's assistance.
facts_and_myths.explanation: When players max out the Extreme Measures condition in the Pact of Punishment, Hades gains a high-difficulty third phase with an all-new heavy metal musical theme.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Hades's majestic cape dissolves into a river of skulls whenever he summons boiling blood or enters stealth mode during combat.

facts_and_myths.claim: Hades is depicted by Supergiant Games as an outright evil, sadistic villain who hates his son without reason.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Hades is portrayed with deep nuance as an emotionally guarded, grieving father burdened by duty, who acts harsh primarily to test Zagreus and protect family secrets.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Voice actor Logan Cunningham voiced Lord Hades, the Narrator, Poseidon, Achilles, Charon, and Asterius all in the same game.

name: Cuphead
visual_anchor: A cheerful vintage 1930s rubber hose cartoon cup-headed character wearing red shorts and white gloves, firing glowing finger bullets against whimsical watercolor carnival backdrops in high resolution vertical frame.
core_traits: Protagonist of a notorious retro run-and-gun platformer known for extreme hand-drawn boss fights
Traveled across Inkwell Isle alongside brother Mugman after losing a fateful wager to the Devil
Attacks enemies by finger-snapping magical energy projectiles while executing precision pink parries
Features authentic 1930s Fleischer-style rubber hose animation and big band jazz orchestration

facts_and_myths.claim: Cuphead visual art style was created using genuine traditional 1930s hand-drawn animation techniques on paper.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Studio MDHR painstakingly hand-drew every animation frame on paper with pencil and inking before digital coloring and compositing.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The developers mortgaged their homes to expand the development scope into a full boss-rush platforming spectacle.

facts_and_myths.claim: Cuphead was originally intended to be a turn-based role playing game.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Cuphead was conceived from day one as a twitch-reflex run-and-gun boss-rush platformer inspired by Gunstar Heroes and Contra III.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: A special uncompressed jazz big band recorded the entire energetic soundtrack live in studio.

name: Mugman
visual_anchor: A cautious cartoon boy with a porcelain mug for a head and a broad blue nose, wearing blue shorts and brown boots, dodging explosive watercolor projectiles with a wide expressive grin in 9:16 vertical view.
core_traits: The cautious and thoughtful brother of Cuphead who acts as second player in cooperative play
Distinguished by his large spherical blue nose and calm demeanor compared to his impulsive sibling
Assisted Cuphead in collecting soul contracts across Inkwell Isle to save their own souls from the Devil
Equipped with identical finger-gun projectile magic and acrobatic pink parry abilities

facts_and_myths.claim: Mugman was voiced by an entirely different sound designer who recorded unique vocal grunts.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Audio cues and distinctive vocalizations for Mugman were separately tracked to provide subtle auditory distinction between co-op players.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: In the Netflix animated series, Mugman is portrayed as the anxious voice of reason constantly reining in Cuphead reckless plans.

facts_and_myths.claim: Mugman has a slower running speed than Cuphead to balance co-op gameplay.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Both Cuphead and Mugman possess completely identical hitboxes, movement speeds, jump heights, and weapon firing rates in the core game.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Player two can freely revive a fallen ghost teammate by parrying their rising spirit before it floats offscreen.

name: Shovel Knight
visual_anchor: A chivalrous warrior clad in lustrous cerulean armor clutching an engraved steel digging shovel like an enchanted broadsword, standing victorious upon crumbling 8-bit stone ramparts in dramatic vertical lighting.
core_traits: Heroic blue-armored warrior who wields the ShovelBlade to vanquish foes and unearth buried treasure
Set out on an epic quest to defeat the Order of No Quarter and rescue his lost partner Shield Knight
Pioneered the retro-indie Renaissance with authentic 8-bit NES aesthetic and down-thrust digging attacks
Created by Yacht Club Games, becoming an iconic guest fighter across dozens of indie crossovers

facts_and_myths.claim: Shovel Knight downward shovel thrust mechanic was directly inspired by DuckTales and Zelda II.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Designers at Yacht Club Games specifically modeled the shovel bounce on Scrooge McDuck cane bounce and Link downward sword stab.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The game soundtrack featured guest compositions from legendary Mega Man composer Manami Matsumae.

facts_and_myths.claim: Shovel Knight was originally created as a licensed game prototype for an animated Saturday morning cartoon.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Shovel Knight was an original independent concept conceived by former WayForward developers following a successful Kickstarter campaign in 2013.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: An official Shovel Knight amiibo was produced by Nintendo, marking the first indie game character with full amiibo hardware support.

name: Madeline
visual_anchor: A determined young woman with glowing strawberry-red hair dashing through blizzard winds on jagged alpine cliffs, surrounded by sparkling floating feather powerups in vertical mountain vista.
core_traits: Resilient protagonist of the acclaimed precision platformer Celeste who climbs Celeste Mountain
Confronts and ultimately reconciles with her inner manifestation of panic and self-doubt named Badeline
Possesses acrobatic mid-air dash mechanics that recharge upon touching solid ground or green crystals
Explores deeply emotional themes of mental health, anxiety management, and self-acceptance

facts_and_myths.claim: Celeste began development as a four-day game jam project for the fantasy console PICO-8.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Maddy Thorson and Noel Berry built the original 30-level Celeste prototype in roughly four days using the simulated 8-bit PICO-8 system.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The full Celeste game contains an easter egg that lets players play the original PICO-8 prototype inside a secret mountain room.

facts_and_myths.claim: Madeline can perform unlimited dashes by default without touching the ground or crystals.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Madeline is strictly limited to a single eight-directional dash until Chapter 7, where she unlocks a second dash after reconciling with Badeline.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The game has been widely embraced by speedrunners who exploit advanced physics techniques like hyper-dashing and wave-dashing.

name: Isaac
visual_anchor: A wide-eyed bald cartoon child weeping glowing blue projectile tears, clutching a protective holy clover while trapped in a shadowy cobblestone cellar surrounded by macabre dungeon relics in vertical layout.
core_traits: Unfortunate child protagonist of the roguelike masterpiece The Binding of Isaac designed by Edmund McMillen
Escapes his fanatical mother by diving into an ever-shifting subterranean dungeon beneath his bedroom
Weaponizes his own copious tears as directional projectiles against monstrous basement aberrations
Features hundreds of synergistic passive items, biblical allegories, and unlockable transformation states

facts_and_myths.claim: The Binding of Isaac was initially developed in Flash before being completely rebuilt for Rebirth.
facts_and_myths.explanation: The original 2011 game was created in Flash in three months; Rebirth completely rebuilt the engine in C++ with a 16-bit art style to remove performance caps.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The title and narrative premise directly satirize the biblical narrative of Abraham and Isaac on Mount Moriah.

facts_and_myths.claim: Isaac can only carry a maximum of two passive items in any single roguelike run.
facts_and_myths.explanation: There is no hard limit on passive item collection in Isaac; players can stack dozens of synergistic items that wildly warp appearance and tears.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The game spawned an entire subgenre of dual-stick procedural bullet-hell roguelikes.

name: Goose
visual_anchor: A mischievous pure white goose with bright orange bill and webbed feet waddling across an idyllic English village garden carrying a stolen silver bell in vertical comedic frame.
core_traits: Unruly feathered protagonist of House House smash hit comedy stealth game Untitled Goose Game
Terrorizes an unsuspecting quaint English village by stealing items, honking loudly, and tripping locals
Maintains a meticulous to-do list notebook filled with hilariously antisocial rural pranks
Features dynamic interactive piano ragtime music that synchronizes with the waterfowl mischief

facts_and_myths.claim: The developers chose the game title as a temporary placeholder that became too popular to change.
facts_and_myths.explanation: House House labeled their early gameplay trailer Untitled Goose Game, and the viral reception made the moniker permanent.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The game won Game of the Year at the 20th Game Developers Choice Awards and the BAFTA Games Awards.

facts_and_myths.claim: The Goose gains flying abilities after completing the village to-do list tasks.
facts_and_myths.explanation: The Goose remains strictly flightless throughout the entire game, relying entirely on running, swimming, hiding in boxes, and honking.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Dedicated button commands exist purely to honk, bend the neck forward, and spread wings menacingly.

name: Guide
visual_anchor: A rustic pixel-art woodsman in leather vest and brown boots holding a wooden bow beside a log cabin at dusk, overlooking a sprawling 2D cavern world in vertical composition.
core_traits: The very first non-player character who spawns beside the player in the 2D sandbox world of Terraria
Provides vital crafting recipes and beginner survival tips when shown raw building materials
Sacrificing his life via the Guide Voodoo Doll in the Underworld awakens the monstrous Wall of Flesh
His sacrifice is the mandatory gateway that unlocks Hardmode across the entire world

facts_and_myths.claim: Throwing the Guide Voodoo Doll into underworld lava instantly kills the Guide and summons the Wall of Flesh.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Lava contact with the Voodoo Doll consumes the Guide NPC wherever he is currently residing and begins the climactic boss confrontation.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: If the Guide is killed through normal means, he respawns the following morning under an alternate random name.

facts_and_myths.claim: The Guide sells high-tier hardmode weapons directly to the player for gold coins.
facts_and_myths.explanation: The Guide never sells goods or trades currency; his exclusive functions are dispensing advice and displaying complete crafting trees.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Terraria has sold over 58 million copies worldwide, ranking among the top best-selling video games in history.

name: Wilson
visual_anchor: An eccentric gothic cartoon scientist with jagged dark hair and a formal vest shivering beside a flickering campfire in a grim Tim Burton-style wilderness in vertical aspect.
core_traits: Dapper gentleman scientist who serves as the flagship playable survivor in Klei Entertainment Don't Starve
Tricked by the sinister antagonist Maxwell into constructing an arcane portal to the hostile Constant
Grows a magnificent protective beard that provides crucial insulation against winter freezing
Must balance hunger, physical health, and psychological sanity against shadow creatures

facts_and_myths.claim: Wilson magnificent beard can be shaved with a razor to collect beard hair for Meat Effigies.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Shaving Wilson beard yields beard hair, which is a required crafting component to build resurrective Meat Effigy respawn totems.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Wilson voice is uniquely synthesized using recordings of a vintage brass trumpet.

facts_and_myths.claim: Wilson is completely immune to psychological sanity loss during pitch-black nights.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Wilson suffers standard sanity depletion in complete darkness and around night monsters like most baseline survivors in the game.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: His full name is Wilson Percival Higgsbury, and he prides himself on adhering to empirical scientific method even amidst nightmare monsters.

name: Impostor
visual_anchor: A sinister red spacesuit astronaut revealing sharp alien fangs and a deadly extendable tongue inside an emergency reactor room bathed in flashing crimson emergency sirens in vertical frame.
core_traits: Deceptive parasitic alien antagonist disguising itself among space crewmates in social deduction phenomenon Among Us
Sabotages critical ship systems including reactor meltdowns, oxygen deprivation, and electrical blackouts
Navigates the spaceship secretly through ventilation ducts while waiting to assassinate isolated astronauts
Engages in psychological deceit, misdirection, and false accusations during emergency meetings

facts_and_myths.claim: Among Us experienced unprecedented viral global explosion nearly two years after its original quiet release in 2018.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Released quietly in 2018 with modest player counts, Among Us exploded into a multi-billion hour cultural phenomenon in mid-2020 due to Twitch and YouTube streamers.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The game was developed by InnerSloth, an indie studio that originally consisted of just three people.

facts_and_myths.claim: The Impostor can repair the critical reactor and oxygen sabotages that they triggered themselves.
facts_and_myths.explanation: While Impostors can interact with sabotage panels to feign innocence, failing to resolve them before the timer runs out awards victory to the Impostors regardless.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The word Sus entered mainstream internet lexicon worldwide primarily as a direct result of Among Us gameplay.

name: Crewmate
visual_anchor: A small colorful bean-shaped astronaut in a cyan spacesuit frantically swiping an admin ID card at a spaceship terminal under glowing fluorescent lights in vertical aspect.
core_traits: Dedicated astronaut protagonist in InnerSloth multiplayer party game Among Us
Completes various mini-game maintenance chores such as rewiring circuits, emptying garbage, and aligning engines
Reports dead bodies and convenes emergency meetings to debate and vote suspected shapeshifters off the ship
Can continue completing assigned ship maintenance tasks as a benevolent floating ghost after demise

facts_and_myths.claim: Defeated Crewmates become translucent ghosts who can freely pass through walls and complete remaining tasks.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Ghost players cannot speak during meetings, but completing all of their remaining tasks still contributes to a total crew task victory.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: InnerSloth canceled their planned sequel Among Us 2 in order to pour all development focus into expanding the original game.

facts_and_myths.claim: Crewmates can carry weapons to directly battle and defeat an attacking Impostor in real time.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Crewmates possess zero weapons or physical combat abilities; their sole defenses are keen observation, surveillance cameras, and democratic voting.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The characteristic spacesuit design was chosen by the artist purely because it was quick and easy to draw repeatedly.
